newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore rubber ends up on buying for RSS3 rubber.
newsitem.headline: Singapore rubber ends up on buying for RSS3 rubber.

text.p: The Singapore rubber market closed higher on Monday as players engaged in a bout of buying in anticipation of more purchases by China of RSS3 grade rubber, dealers said.
"There's talk going around that China will finish talks with Thailand to buy more RSS3 rubber. That was taken as a signal to buy by some people in the market," a dealer said
Dealers said the volume of rubber could reach as much as 80,000 tonnes for shipment during the second half of the year.
"The physical side was pretty quiet, but activity picked up during the ring sessions," a dealer said.

Traders said Singapore-based buyers also recently picked up several hundred tonnes of SIR20 rubber at around 47-48 U.S. cents a kg FOB Palembang while others engaged in forward purchases for RSS1 grade rubber.
"Trading for the other rubber grades remained pretty thin. It's still a slow market out there even though activity should perk up soon," a dealer said.
At 0945 GMT, July RSS3 was seen at 115.50-117.50 U.S. cents a kg from 115.50 cents. April/June RSS1 was seen at 172.00 Singapore cents (US$1.20) a kg from 170.50 cents.
